summary: Summation No. 31 covers April 1948 (statistics mostly for February-March). Politically, government employees' unions accepted the 2,920-yen wage scale on 16 April after SCAP forbade a communications strike; the Ashida coalition was strained by the Social Democratic demand to suspend war bond interest, cabinet disagreement over labor law revision, and the Tsuji hoarded-goods inquiry. Korean protests against school closures in Osaka and Kobe required Occupation troops. The Diet created the Maritime Safety Board and restored parliamentary vice-ministers; the purge continued and the IMTFE heard final defense summations. Economically, March output hit postwar highs in steel, chemicals, rayon, cotton and silk fabrics, with coal at 2.86 million tons, while the February trade deficit was $60.9 million. Finance, rationing, labor, health, education and media statistics follow. Historians will find detailed tables on production, trade, repatriation and the war crimes trials.
highlights: Government employees' unions accepted the 2,920-yen wage scale on 16 April, ending their dispute, after SCAP three times barred a general strike by communications workers.
The Social Democrats' demand to suspend war bond interest strained the Ashida coalition, alongside Cabinet disagreement over labor-law revision and the Tsuji hoarded-goods inquiry.
Koreans protested school closures in Osaka and Kobe on 23-26 April; 23 Koreans and 58 police were injured, 183 arrested, and Occupation troops helped disperse the Kobe crowds.
The Diet passed the Maritime Safety Authorities Bill on 15 April, authorizing up to 10,000 men and 125 vessels, and 22 parliamentary vice-ministers were appointed.
IMTFE defense summations for all 25 accused were completed 15 April, and the court adjourned 16 April to prepare its judgment.

March output set postwar highs in steel, chemicals, rayon, cotton and silk fabrics, with coal at 2,862,500 tons; the February trade deficit was $60.9 million, 73 percent of imports from the United States.
By 17 April 711,036 persons had been screened in the purge, with 4,880 removed and 2,876 barred; 189,162 were finally designated.
764,900 persons were still awaiting repatriation to Japan, while 396 returned in April, bringing the total to 5,843,095.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover of Summation No. 31 (April 1948), contents for Parts I to IV (General, Political, Economic, Social) and a list of charts, maps and graphs ending with the Map of Japan.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Paragraph-numbered digest: the Restitution Advisory Committee (13 April), government employees' 2,920-yen wage settlement, March production gains, February trade deficit of $60.9 million, and 764,900 persons awaiting repatriation.

sections.title: Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: The Restitution Advisory Committee was established 13 April to advise the Supreme Commander on looted property found in Japan; the Civil Property Custodian chairs it, with delegates from participating Far Eastern Commission nations.

sections.title: Political Activities
sections.summary: Government employees accepted the 2,920-yen wage scale; Cabinet split on labor-law changes; war bond interest went to interparty talks; Tsuji fund inquiry, 18 bills, purge totals, Korean school protests and the Maritime Safety bill also noted.

sections.title: Economic Activities
sections.summary: March output rose in coal, steel, chemicals and bicycles (47,120). February imports of $70.3 million against exports of $9.4 million left a $60.9 million deficit; note circulation reached 220.4 billion yen; 7,805 machine tools shipped as reparations.

sections.title: Social Activities
sections.summary: Japanese B encephalitis research began at the National Institute of Health, penicillin output rose 138 percent, 764,900 persons awaited repatriation, and 94,650,553 textbooks were authorized, with 647 million yen for lower secondary schools.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics, public safety, and legal affairs: wage dispute settlement and war bond interest controversy, Korean school riots in Osaka and Kobe, and the final IMTFE defense summations.

sections.title: Government and Politics
sections.summary: The government-employee wage dispute ended, the war bond interest controversy and Tsuji hoarded-goods inquiry continued, party positions shifted, the Diet enacted 18 laws, and the purge screened 711,036 persons.

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.summary: The 2,920-yen dispute ended 16 April after SCAP three times barred communications strikes; Ashida and Labor Minister Kato clashed over labor law. Also: war bond interest conference, Tsuji inquiry, Vice-minister Ino's bribery arrest.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: The Democratic Party defined 'modified capitalism' and lost three members to the Democratic Liberals; Social Democrats defended war bond interest suspension and gained to 123 lower house seats; the People's Cooperative Party backed the Cabinet.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: SCAP urged curbs on Diet absenteeism; Ashida asked to extend the session to end of May. The Diet enacted 18 laws including the Coal Board and Maritime Safety bills; 22 parliamentary vice-ministers were appointed 15 April.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: By 17 April 711,036 persons were screened, 4,880 removed and 2,876 barred; 189,162 finally designated. The Appeals Board rejected 135 appeals; the Special Investigation Bureau was organized 20 April with nine regional headquarters.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.summary: Korean-school protests in Osaka (23-26 April) left 23 Koreans and 58 police injured and 183 arrested; Occupation Forces helped disperse Kobe crowds. February saw 149,885 offenses and 79,220 arrests; prison population was 87,233.

sections.title: Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: The Supreme Court upheld capital punishment 12 March. By 20 April 610 war criminals were tried (572 convicted, 94 sentenced to death). IMTFE defense summations for all 25 accused ended 15 April; the court adjourned 16 April to prepare judgment.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Statistics and narrative on production, trade, labor, prices, finance, property and science: March coal 2.86 million tons, postwar highs in steel and textiles, February trade deficit $60.9 million, 6,243,017 union members.

sections.title: Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Land sales to tenants reached 146,558 cho in March (427,320 cumulative); 12,051 agricultural cooperatives held preliminary meetings. February marine production totaled 110,464 tons; Antarctic whaling yielded 17,544.6 long tons of whale oil.

sections.title: Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: March log production rose to 88,984,500 cubic feet; 1947 cutting outran replanting (866,170 against 430,810 cho). March coal output was 2,862,500 tons with 516,897 mine employees; crude oil 16,016 kiloliters.

sections.title: Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Steel set postwar records in March: pig iron 44,777 tons, rolled steel 76,927 tons. Coke reached 221,910 tons, cement 131,669 tons, ammonium sulfate 66,186 tons; aluminum fell to 374 tons.

sections.title: Manufacturing
sections.summary: February flour output jumped 290 percent to 103,066 tons; March paper reached 34,492 tons, three-wheelers a postwar high of 1,093 and bicycles a record 47,120; trucks fell to 942 chassis.

sections.title: Textile Industries
sections.summary: March textile output rose, with postwar peaks in rayon, cotton and silk fabrics. Cotton yarn reached 23,181,000 pounds; cotton cloth topped 65.7 million square yards; raw silk rose 1,236 bales to 10,106.

sections.title: Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Registered commercial vehicles rose to 163,766 (67.5 percent operable). Government railways carried 303,921,713 passengers, up 9.5 percent, and 9,861,800 metric tons of freight; electric generation was 2,607,867,000 kilowatt hours.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: Telephones in service rose 1.3 percent to 1,195,238; new radio links opened to Latin America, Europe and Asia. Radio households reached 6,443,206; a Diet appropriation of 3,289,493,000 yen was noted.

sections.title: Labor
sections.summary: Government workers' dispute ended 16 April with acceptance of the 2,920-yen wage level and a 15-grade pay plan. Unions numbered 29,378 with 6,243,017 members; February disputes involved 189,558 workers.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: February imports of $70,261,684 and exports of $9,400,019 left a deficit near $60.9 million. About 73 percent of imports came from the United States; textiles were 41 percent of exports.

sections.title: Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: April rations were met from carryover stocks after 1947 crop quotas were fulfilled in March (rice 100.1 percent); the substitute-rice program ended. February family expenditures were 6,214 yen; 6,646 enforcement cases reported.

sections.title: Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes outstanding reached 220.44 billion yen on 30 April. Reconstruction Finance Bank loans stood at 59.46 billion yen; 1947-48 tax receipts were 124.9 billion yen; national debt 360.8 billion yen.

sections.title: Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: Looted property worth 3.76 million yen was taken into custody; 353 looted ships were reported, 55 percent sunk. SCAP approved 282 restricted-concern transactions; advance reparations shipments reached 7,805 machine tools.

sections.title: Science and Technology
sections.summary: The Renewal Committee for the Organization of Science held its final meeting 25-27 March, recommending a Science Council under the Prime Minister's office. Japanese Standards reached 1,009; 175 patents were granted.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, and education, religion, cultural resources and media: typhoid inoculations, penicillin record, 3,077,031 persons on welfare aid, repatriation, textbook authorization and public opinion surveys.

sections.title: Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: About 36.4 million typhoid inoculations were given by 26 April; a 98-case typhus outbreak at an Osaka hospital was contained. Penicillin hit a record 157,019 vials; 396 repatriates returned in April (5,843,095 total).

sections.title: Education, Religion, Cultural Resources and Media of Expression
sections.summary: A 647 million yen supplementary budget for lower secondary schools, 12,123 new lower secondary schools, and 94.7 million textbooks authorized. Public opinion surveys, press, radio and films are covered; a Fukuoka SCAP library closes the section.
